questions.question: In which year did the ‘Battle of Buxar’ take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1764 CE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The '**Battle of Buxar**' took place in the year **1764 CE**.
 
• This battle was fought between the **British East India Company** and the **combined forces of the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, the Nawab of Bengal Mir Qasim, and the Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daula**.
 
• The battle was a significant event in Indian history as it established **British control over Bengal and Bihar**, leading to the expansion of British rule in India.
 
• The victory at Buxar allowed the British East India Company to gain the** Diwani rights**, which gave them the authority to **collect revenue from the eastern provinces of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 'Battle of Buxar' was a **follow-up to the 'Battle of Plassey' in 1757**, where the British East India Company had earlier defeated Siraj-ud-Daula, the Nawab of Bengal.
 
• The success in these battles laid the foundation for British colonial rule in India.
 
• The **Treaty of Allahabad** was signed in **1765**, following the Battle of Buxar, which further consolidated British power in the region.
 
• These events marked the beginning of nearly two centuries of British dominance in India.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates that the state should protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 49**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 49** of the Indian Constitution mandates that the **state should protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest**.
 
• This Article falls under the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• The purpose of these principles is to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• It emphasizes the preservation of the rich cultural heritage of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Constitution, from **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• These principles are** not enforceable by any court**, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life and promote the welfare of the people.

questions.question: Alarmel Valli is a __________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alarmel Valli** is an acclaimed Indian classical dancer known for her expertise in **Bharatnatyam**.
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is one of the **oldest classical dance forms** of India, originating from the state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is characterized by its fixed upper torso, bent legs and knees flexed out combined with spectacular footwork, and sophisticated vocabulary of hand and facial gestures.
 
• Alarmel Valli has been awarded several prestigious accolades for her contribution to the art form, including the **Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The origins of Bharatnatyam can be traced back to the **Natya Shastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts.
 
• It is traditionally performed by women, and has its roots in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• The dance form was revived in the early 20th century by pioneers like **Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer**.
 
• In modern times, Bharatnatyam is performed by both men and women and has gained global recognition.
 
• Bharatnatyam performances typically involve a solo dancer who performs a variety of items, each with a distinct mood and meaning.

questions.question: The Sirpur Shrine is situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__

__
 
• The **Sirpur Shrine** is located in the state of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• Sirpur, also known as Shripur, is a small village situated on the banks of the **Mahanadi River in the Mahasamund district of Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It is an important archaeological site and was once a prominent center for **Buddhism and Hinduism**.
 
• The site includes various ancient temples, monasteries, and other structures dating back to the 6th to 10th centuries.
 
• Sirpur is famous for its intricate carvings and architectural marvels, attracting historians, archaeologists, and tourists alike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhattisgarh** is a state located in central India, known for its rich cultural heritage and natural resources.
 
• The state was formed on **1st November 2000**, after being **separated from Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Chhattisgarh is known for its diverse tribal culture, ancient monuments, and natural beauty, including waterfalls, caves, and forests.
 
• The capital city of Chhattisgarh is **Raipur**.
 
• The state has several other important historical and archaeological sites, such as the Bhoramdeo Temple and the Kanker Palace.

questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the climate of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Altitude**, **latitude**, and **winds** are significant factors affecting the climate of India.
 
• **Longitude** does not have a direct impact on the climate of India.
 
• **Altitude affects temperature and precipitation patterns**.
 
• **Latitude **influences the amount of solar energy received, affecting temperature and climate zones.
 
• Winds play a crucial role in the distribution of heat and moisture, affecting weather patterns and climate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's climate is influenced by multiple factors including geographic location, topography, and atmospheric conditions.
 
• The Indian subcontinent experiences diverse climatic conditions ranging from tropical in the south to temperate and alpine in the north.
 
• The Himalayas play a significant role in shaping the climate by **blocking cold winds from Central Asia**.
 
• The monsoon winds are a critical component of India's climate, bringing significant rainfall during the summer months.

questions.question: What is the common name for a saturated solution of calcium hydroxide widely used as a raw material in the chemical industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slaked lime**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slaked lime** is the common name for a **saturated solution of calcium hydroxide**.
 
• It is widely used as a raw material in the chemical industry for various applications.
 
• Calcium hydroxide, also known as **hydrated lime**, is produced by adding water to **quicklime **(calcium oxide).
 
• Slaked lime is used in the production of **mortar and plaster**, in water and sewage treatment, and in the paper industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium hydroxide** has a chemical formula of **Ca(OH)₂**.
 
• It is a **colorless crystal or white powder**.
 
• Slaked lime is slightly soluble in water and forms a solution known as limewater, which is used to test for the presence of carbon dioxide.
 
• When carbon dioxide is passed through limewater, it turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate.

questions.question: Who led the Congress in the second round table conference held in London?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** led the Congress delegation in the **second round table conference** held in **London**.
 
• The second round table conference took place from **7th September 1931 to 1st December 1931**.
 
• This conference aimed to discuss constitutional reforms in India and included representatives from various Indian political and social groups.
 
• **Gandhi represented the Indian National Congress and was the sole representative of the Congress at this conference**.
 
• The conference, however, did not result in any significant progress towards Indian self-rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **first round table conference** was held from **November 1930 to January 1931**, and the **third round table conference** was held from **November to December 1932**.
 
• The round table conferences were a series of peace conferences organized by the British Government to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** was eventually passed, incorporating some of the discussions from these conferences.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's participation in the second round table conference was significant as it marked his first and only visit to London after the start of the freedom struggle in India.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which state has the second highest sex ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu** has the **second highest sex ratio** according to the **Census of India 2011**.
 
• The sex ratio is an important demographic indicator that reflects the **number of females per 1000 males** in a population.
 
• **Kerala **holds the **highest sex ratio** among the Indian states, followed by Tamil Nadu.
 
• Improving the sex ratio is a critical aspect of achieving gender equality and addressing issues related to gender imbalances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Census of India** is conducted every ten years and is the most comprehensive source of demographic data in the country.
 
• The **2011 Census** was the **15th National Census since 1871** and provided detailed data on population distribution, sex ratio, literacy rates, and other key metrics.
 
• Efforts to improve the sex ratio include initiatives like **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao** (Save the Daughter, Educate the Daughter) which aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote gender equality.
 
• Continuous monitoring and targeted policies are essential to address the factors contributing to the skewed sex ratio, such as gender-based discrimination and preferences for male children.

questions.question: Factor cost is also known as:
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'input cost'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Understanding Factor Cost:**

 
 
• Factor cost refers to the cost of the factors of production used in the production of goods and services.
 
• It includes all costs associated with the inputs used in the production process, such as labor, raw materials, and capital.
 
• In economics, factor cost is often termed as input cost because it represents the expenses incurred in obtaining the necessary inputs for production.
 
• Factor cost does not include taxes and other levies that may be added to the final price of a product.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comparison with Other Costs:**

 
 
• **Option 1 (Market Cost):**

 
 
• Market cost includes all expenses related to producing and selling a good or service, including profit margins, and is not synonymous with factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Option 2 (Ex-factory Cost):**
 
 
• This term refers to the cost of goods at the factory gate, excluding transportation and distribution costs, and does not equate to factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Option 4 (Output Cost):**
 
 
• Output cost refers to the total cost of producing a particular level of output, including fixed and variable costs, which may extend beyond just factor costs.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Understanding factor cost is crucial for analyzing production costs and determining pricing strategies in business.
 
• It serves as a foundational concept in economic theories relating to production, cost analysis, and pricing mechanisms.
 
• Recognizing the difference between factor cost and other cost types helps businesses and economists make informed decisions regarding resource allocation and production efficiency.

questions.question: Which cell found in the bone marrow acts as a repair system for the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stem cells**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stem cells** are found in the **bone marrow** and **act as a repair system for the body**.
 
• These cells have the unique ability to develop into different types of cells in the body, including** bone cells, fat cells, and muscle cells**.
 
• Stem cells play a crucial role in the body's ability to heal and regenerate tissues.
 
• They can divide and produce new stem cells (self-renewal) or differentiate into specialized cells (differentiation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bone marrow** is a spongy tissue found in the center of bones, particularly in the hip and thigh bones.
 
• It is responsible for producing blood cells, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, through a process called **hematopoiesis**.
 
• There are two types of stem cells found in the bone marrow: **hematopoietic stem cells** (which give rise to blood cells) and **mesenchymal stem cells** (which can develop into bone, cartilage, and fat cells).
 
• Stem cell research holds significant potential for developing treatments for various diseases and injuries, including leukemia, lymphoma, and spinal cord injuries.

questions.question: When was the first general election for Lok Sabha held in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951-52**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first general election for Lok Sabha** in India was held in **1951-52**.
 
• This election was the first major electoral exercise conducted in Independent India, marking the establishment of a democratic government.
 
• The elections were held under the provisions of the Indian Constitution, which came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It was a landmark event as it was conducted based on universal adult suffrage, allowing every **Indian citizen aged 21 and above to vote**.
 
• The Indian National Congress emerged as the winning party in this historic election.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Adult Suffrage** was a significant feature of this election, making it one of the largest democratic exercises in the world at that time.
 
• The election process was overseen by the Election Commission of India, established in **1950**.
 
• The first general election set the stage for the practice of regular, free, and fair elections in India, reinforcing democratic values.
 
• The successful conduct of the election was a testament to the administrative capabilities of the newly independent nation.
 
• The first Lok Sabha had a tenure from **1952 to 1957**, with Dr. Rajendra Prasad serving as the President of India and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru as the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India is the first to receive rainfall from the South West Monsoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** is the first state in India to receive rainfall from the **South West Monsoon**.
 
• The onset of the South West Monsoon typically occurs in Kerala **around the beginning of June**.
 
• This marks the start of the monsoon season in India, which gradually progresses to other parts of the country.
 
• The South West Monsoon is crucial for the Indian subcontinent, providing the majority of the annual rainfall and supporting agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The South West Monsoon winds are driven by the **differential heating of land and sea**, along with the **Coriolis effect**.
 
• The monsoon is divided into two branches:** the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch**, both of which contribute to the rainfall in various regions of India.
 
• The arrival and strength of the monsoon are monitored by the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
 
• Monsoon rains are vital for replenishing water resources, supporting agriculture, and maintaining ecological balance in the region.
 
• Variability in monsoon patterns can have significant impacts on agriculture, water supply, and overall economic activity in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is a famous novel written by Munshi Premchand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Godan** is a renowned novel written by **Munshi Premchand**, a celebrated Indian author.
 
• It was published in **1936 **and is considered one of the greatest works in Hindi literature.
 
• The novel provides a critical portrayal of the socio-economic conditions of rural India during the early 20th century.
 
• Through its protagonist Hori Mahato, the novel explores themes of poverty, exploitation, and the struggle for dignity among the rural peasantry.
 
• **Godan** is recognized for its realistic depiction and profound narrative, making it a classic in Indian literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Munshi Premchand**, born Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, is often referred to as the "**Upanyas Samrat**" (Emperor of Novels) in Hindi literature.
 
• His works primarily focus on the lives of the poor and marginalized sections of society, highlighting social injustices and human suffering.
